claims.title: The temples of Ggantija raised on Gozo
claims.summary: The two megalithic temples of Ggantija were built on Gozo, the South Temple around 3600 BCE, ranking among the oldest free-standing monumental buildings in the world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-3600bce-the-temples-of-ggantija-raised-on-gozo, claim TL:MLT:event:3600bce:the-temples-of-ggantija-raised-on-gozo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Maltese temple culture flourishes
claims.summary: A Neolithic society raised the temples of Hagar Qim, Mnajdra, Tarxien, Skorba and Ta' Hagrat in successive phases, creating monumental architecture without the use of metal tools.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-3600bce-the-maltese-temple-culture-flourishes, claim TL:MLT:event:3600bce:the-maltese-temple-culture-flourishes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Hal Saflieni Hypogeum
claims.summary: A vast underground necropolis was cut on three levels into the limestone, holding the remains of about 7,000 people and the famous Sleeping Lady figurine.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-3000bce-the-hal-saflieni-hypogeum, claim TL:MLT:event:3000bce:the-hal-saflieni-hypogeum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The temple builders disappear
claims.summary: Around 2500 BCE the temple-building culture came to an end for reasons still debated, and a new Bronze Age population succeeded the people who had raised the great monuments.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-2500bce-the-temple-builders-disappear, claim TL:MLT:event:2500bce:the-temple-builders-disappear, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Carthaginian Malta
claims.summary: Following earlier Phoenician use of the islands as a trading station, the Carthaginians were firmly established in Malta by the sixth century BCE, leaving coins, inscriptions and Punic rock tombs.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-600bce-carthaginian-malta, claim TL:MLT:event:600bce:carthaginian-malta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malta becomes Roman
claims.summary: During the Second Punic War Malta passed under Roman control and was attached to the praetorship of Sicily, beginning some seven centuries of Roman and then Byzantine rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-218bce-malta-becomes-roman, claim TL:MLT:event:218bce:malta-becomes-roman, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The shipwreck of the Apostle Paul
claims.summary: Christian tradition, drawing on the Acts of the Apostles, holds that Paul was shipwrecked on Malta around 60 CE, welcomed by the islanders and the leading man Publius, and stayed three months, beginning the islands' conversion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-60-the-shipwreck-of-the-apostle-paul, claim TL:MLT:event:60:the-shipwreck-of-the-apostle-paul, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Roman municipium
claims.summary: Under Rome the Maltese were allowed to coin money, send delegations to Rome and manage their own affairs, and the islands were granted the status of a Roman municipium.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-100-roman-municipium, claim TL:MLT:event:100:roman-municipium, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arab conquest of Malta
claims.summary: An Arab force seized Malta from the Byzantine Empire, beginning a period of more than two centuries that would shape the islands' language and culture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-870-arab-conquest-of-malta, claim TL:MLT:event:870:arab-conquest-of-malta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Birth of the Maltese language
claims.summary: The Arabic of the islands' settlers evolved into Maltese, a Semitic language that is unique in being written in the Latin alphabet and that survives as the national language today.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-900-birth-of-the-maltese-language, claim TL:MLT:event:900:birth-of-the-maltese-language, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Norman conquest by Roger I
claims.summary: Count Roger I of Sicily took Malta from the Arabs in 1091, attaching the islands to the Kingdom of Sicily and beginning their return to Latin Christendom.

sources.label: Roger I, Norman Count of Sicily

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1091-norman-conquest-by-roger-i, claim TL:MLT:event:1091:norman-conquest-by-roger-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rule under Sicily and Aragon
claims.summary: As part of the Kingdom of Sicily, Malta passed through Norman, Swabian, Angevin and Aragonese hands, governed by feudal lords and a local council, until 1530.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1283-rule-under-sicily-and-aragon, claim TL:MLT:event:1283:rule-under-sicily-and-aragon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Charles V grants Malta to the Knights
claims.summary: Eight years after losing Rhodes to the Ottomans, the Order of St John received Malta from the Emperor Charles V, who held Sicily, in return for a token annual tribute, and made the islands their new sovereign base.

sources.label: History of the Order of Malta: 1048 to Present

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1530-charles-v-grants-malta-to-the-knights, claim TL:MLT:event:1530:charles-v-grants-malta-to-the-knights, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Great Siege of Malta
claims.summary: An Ottoman army sent by Suleiman the Magnificent besieged the Knights and Maltese for nearly four months; under Grand Master Jean Parisot de la Valette the defenders held out until a Sicilian relief force compelled the Ottomans to withdraw.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1565-the-great-siege-of-malta, claim TL:MLT:event:1565:the-great-siege-of-malta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Valletta
claims.summary: In the year after the siege the Knights began building a new fortified capital on Mount Sciberras, named Valletta after the Grand Master and conceived as a planned Renaissance fortress-city; it became the capital in 1570.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1566-founding-of-valletta, claim TL:MLT:event:1566:founding-of-valletta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Two and a half centuries of the Order
claims.summary: From their new capital the Knights ruled Malta as a sovereign order-state, building auberges, hospitals and the conventual church of St John and shaping a baroque culture until their fall in 1798.

sources.label: History of the Order of Malta: 1048 to Present

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1571-two-and-a-half-centuries-of-the-order, claim TL:MLT:event:1571:two-and-a-half-centuries-of-the-order, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Napoleon seizes Malta
claims.summary: On his way to Egypt, Napoleon Bonaparte captured Malta from the Knights of St John, whose rule collapsed almost without a fight, ending two and a half centuries of the Order's sovereignty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1798-napoleon-seizes-malta, claim TL:MLT:event:1798:napoleon-seizes-malta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Maltese uprising and French surrender
claims.summary: French seizures of church property triggered a Maltese revolt; with British and Sicilian naval support the insurgents blockaded the French garrison in Valletta until it surrendered in 1800.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1798-maltese-uprising-and-french-surrender, claim TL:MLT:event:1798:maltese-uprising-and-french-surrender, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British rule confirmed by the Treaty of Paris
claims.summary: Having acknowledged British sovereignty, the Maltese saw the islands' attachment to Britain confirmed by the Treaty of Paris in 1814, making Malta a Crown colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1814-british-rule-confirmed-by-the-treaty-of-paris, claim TL:MLT:event:1814:british-rule-confirmed-by-the-treaty-of-paris, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malta as a naval fortress
claims.summary: British development of the Grand Harbour dockyard made Malta one of the chief bases of the Royal Navy and the strategic centre of British power in the Mediterranean.

sources.label: Malta: Modern history (British rule and independence)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1815-malta-as-a-naval-fortress, claim TL:MLT:event:1815:malta-as-a-naval-fortress, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The siege of Malta
claims.summary: From 1940 Malta, lying between Sicily and Axis North Africa, was subjected to relentless Italian and German bombing and a near-starvation blockade while its forces struck at Axis supply convoys.

sources.label: George Cross awarded to the island of Malta

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1940-the-siege-of-malta, claim TL:MLT:event:1940:the-siege-of-malta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malta awarded the George Cross
claims.summary: King George VI awarded the George Cross to the whole island of Malta to honour its heroism and endurance under siege, the only time the decoration has been given to an entire population.

sources.label: George Cross awarded to the island of Malta

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1942-malta-awarded-the-george-cross, claim TL:MLT:event:1942:malta-awarded-the-george-cross, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence
claims.summary: Malta became an independent sovereign state within the Commonwealth on 21 September 1964, ending more than a century and a half of British colonial rule.

sources.label: Malta: Modern history (British rule and independence)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1964-independence, claim TL:MLT:event:1964:independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malta becomes a republic
claims.summary: Constitutional amendments made Malta a republic on 13 December 1974, replacing the British monarch with a Maltese president as head of state.

sources.label: Malta: Modern history (British rule and independence)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-1974-malta-becomes-a-republic, claim TL:MLT:event:1974:malta-becomes-a-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Accession to the European Union
claims.summary: Malta joined the European Union on 1 May 2004 in its largest enlargement and adopted the euro on 1 January 2008, completing its integration into Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malta: Crossroads of the Mediterranean, from the world's oldest temples to a modern European republic.", terralore.co/country/MLT/chronicle#ev-2004-accession-to-the-european-union, claim TL:MLT:event:2004:accession-to-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
